indicators.note: includes says the word for race holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a race of people is a nation
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A swimming contest takes on some volunteer competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming race' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Swimming' alone; 'race' is NATION, which 'includes' TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Natation is the formal, Latin-derived word for the sport of swimming.

clue.text: Up and about, a siren having gone off…

indicators.note: a siren that has gone off has been set going, so its letters are set off into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is up and out of bed because an alarm siren sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone off' rearranges the letters of A SIREN; the surface sense of an alarm sounding is the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has arisen has got up from bed and is now up and about.

indicators.note: retires means the word for simpleton goes back, read from end to start

parts.note: a fool is a simpleton

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person withdraws, keeping their distance from others.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue for the surface only; 'being' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof stays distant and cool towards others, just as a standoffish person does.

clue.text: Batting in place of player on square, there is grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a side batting in cricket is said to be in
for can mean instead of, in place of
a man is a playing piece in chess or draughts
a T-square is a draughtsman's square, so T can stand for it

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: batting instead of a fielder on the square, with grass all round.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (batting, square, grass) is all disguise; 'grass' is slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for informing to the police, and a grass is an informer.

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climb in the north is only just being created.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is coming into existence, newly beginning to develop.

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a tribe's traditional costume is coloured blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour but means smutty or risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are indecent ones, and ribald humour is coarse and vulgar in the same way.

indicators.note: back here tells us the word for clock is read in reverse

parts.note: a timer is a clock for measuring time

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the clocks back, as at the end of summer time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests putting clocks back an hour; in fact 'back' reverses TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send, especially money in payment.

clue.text: Vanessa, perhaps, spread to take to the air

parts.note: butter is a spread for bread
to fly is to take to the air

explanation.surface: A woman named Vanessa might spread her wings and take off.
explanation.walkthrough: Vanessa is not a woman but a genus of butterflies, including the red admiral and painted lady; 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanessa is a genus of brightly coloured insects with scaled wings, so a member is an example.

parts.note: a land is a country
a mark is a spot or stain

explanation.surface: A striking feature of a nation's scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent object that stands out in the scenery.

clue.text: Cricketer to act in a huff?

indicators.note: in says the word for acting is placed inside the word for a huff

parts.note: a miff is a fit of pique, a huff
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A question asking whether someone behaves sulkily.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-OFF is a fielding position in cricket, near the bowler on the off side, and by extension the fielder there.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder stationed at that off-side position is named after it.

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home
tone can mean the style or character of something

explanation.surface: A dating suggestion: a building style from before Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'BC' looks like a date, but it is the notes B and C, which are a half step apart in music.
explanation.definitionFit: B to C on a keyboard is the smallest musical interval, a half step, so it is one example.

parts.note: per means through or by means of
the police force

explanation.surface: Having to get something done with the help of the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old-fashioned word meaning necessarily, because it cannot be avoided.

indicators.note: new says the letters of the name are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Asking whether Shakespeare's prince has a new girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HAMLET; the possessive 's adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: The Sword in the Hearth (Browning version)

definitions.text: The Sword in the Hearth (Browning version)

parts.words: The Sword in the Hearth (Browning version)
parts.note: plays on film titles; the long pronged implement held at the fireside, used for browning bread

explanation.surface: Film titles mashed together, The Sword in the Stone and The Browning Version.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes The Sword in the Stone and The Browning Version; the 'sword' is the long fork used to brown bread at a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled fork holds bread before the fire to brown it, like a little sword in the hearth.

clue.text: North African in a loose jacket?

definitions.meaning: a citrus fruit with easy-peeling skin

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes a small orange whose peel is loose, the 'jacket' being its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tangier is so called, and the loose-skinned mandarin orange shares the name.

clue.text: Negative running to ground-almost a disaster!

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for negative
earthing a fox is chasing it into its hole, running it to ground

explanation.surface: A hunted animal is nearly caught, a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running to ground' gives EARTHING, the hunting term for driving a fox into its earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, something that very nearly went wrong.

parts.note: in 'an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth', satisfaction for a wrong is taken with an eye
the second feature of that biblical retribution is a tooth

explanation.surface: A dog shows two signs of contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satisfaction' here means revenge, as in the biblical law of an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth; 'Canine' is a tooth, not a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper pointed tooth below the eye is called a canine.

parts.note: read as therapy that sends a patient well and truly off, into a trance, not care for the rich

explanation.walkthrough: 'well-off' suggests wealthy patients, but here it means sent well and truly off into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapy given under a trance puts the patient 'off', as if asleep.

clue.text: Essence of mince-pie, as I see it

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the word after it is cut up and rearranged

parts.note: to me means in my opinion, as I see it

explanation.surface: Someone declares that mince pies sum up Christmas, in their view.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'mince-pie' hides its split: 'mince' is the anagram signal working on the word beside it, and 'as I see it' gives TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is the perfect embodiment, the quintessence of something.

clue.text: Member of strict set found in less energetic mood

indicators.note: found in says the answer is lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rigorous sect member is discovered feeling lethargic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'less energetic'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the time of Christ.

definitions.meaning: the accent in rhythm or metre

explanation.definitionFit: To keep harping on something is to emphasise it, and the emphasised beat in music or verse carries the same name.
Fast movement is so described, and the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels bore the name.

definitions.meaning: money earned on savings or a stake

explanation.definitionFit: Banks pay it on deposits as earnings, and a pastime you pursue is also one of your pursuits by that name.

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a rod or pole
in means at home

explanation.surface: An artist's favourite seat in their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' is not a seat but an old measure of length, the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

parts.note: politic means prudent and tactful, diplomatic
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: An MP usually moves in diplomatic circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' belongs to the definition, marking an informal word for a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Politico is a colloquial term for a politician, here an MP.

parts.note: in means fashionable
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A stylish action, beyond any doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed confirms a statement as true beyond question.

indicators.note: mad says the letters of the following word go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A caution issued by the hat-maker from Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like part of the character's name but rearranges HATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a menacing warning of harm to come.

definitions.meaning: to plan and bring about something cleverly

explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a military builder in the Royal Engineers, and to contrive a scheme is to plan it as its mastermind.
